nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a compact convex subset of the Euclidean plane with nonempty interior. Then $K$ does not have two distinct equichordal points: there are no points $P \ne Q$ of the plane such that both $P$ and $Q$ are equichordal points of $K$.
nodes.title: Equichordal point theorem

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a subset of the Euclidean plane.
